ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, extend the side BC of rectangle ABCD to point E so that $CE=BD$. Connect AE, intersecting the diagonal BD at point F, and intersecting side CD at point G. If $\angle ADB = 38^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle E$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure: Connect AC. Let the intersection point of AC and BD be O. \\
Since ABCD is a rectangle, \\
it follows that AC=BD, \\
which means OA=OC=OB=OD, \\
Since $\angle ADB=38^\circ$, \\
it implies $\angle BCA=\angle DBC=38^\circ$, \\
Since CE=BD, \\
it leads to AC=CE, \\
Therefore, $\angle E=\boxed{19^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Use an auxiliary diagonal AC and angle chasing. From the image, identify ABCD as a rectangle with B-C-E collinear horizontally, E to the right of C, and diagonal AE forming the requested angle at E; F and G are intersections on AE but are not needed. From the text, use CE=BD and ∠ADB=38°. Draw AC. In a rectangle, the diagonals are equal, so AC=BD; hence AC=CE. Also, because the rectangle has parallel horizontal sides and congruent right-triangle geometry, the angle the diagonal AC makes with CB equals the angle the diagonal BD makes with DA, so ∠BCA=∠ADB=38°. Since CE is the extension of CB in the opposite direction, ∠ACE=180°−38°=142°. Triangle ACE is isosceles with AC=CE, so its base angles at A and E are equal; therefore ∠E=(180°−142°)/2=19°.

推理：按方法作辅助对角线 AC。因为 ABCD 是长方形，所以两条对角线相等，即 AC=BD。题设给出 CE=BD，因此 AC=CE。又因为长方形中 AD ∥ BC，且对角线 AC 与 BD 相对于长方形的水平边形成对应的锐角，所以 ∠BCA=∠ADB=38°。由于 CE 是 CB 的反向延长线，所以 ∠ACE=180°−38°=142°。在三角形 ACE 中，AC=CE，因此它是等腰三角形，底角 ∠CAE 和 ∠AEC 相等。于是 ∠E=∠AEC=(180°−142°)/2=19°。

From the image, set coordinates consistent with the rectangle: B=(0,0), C=(w,0), A=(0,h), D=(w,h), and since E is on the extension of BC, let E=(w+d,0), where d=CE. From the text, d=CE=BD and ∠ADB=38°. In right triangle ADB, BD=sqrt(w^2+h^2), and if θ=∠ADB, then h/w=tan θ, with θ=38°. ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, extend the side BC of rectangle ABCD to point E so that $CE=BD$. Connect AE, intersecting the diagonal BD at point F, and intersecting side CD at point G. If $\angle ADB = 38^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle E$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure: Connect AC. Let the intersection point of AC and BD be O. \\
Since ABCD is a rectangle, \\
it follows that AC=BD, \\
which means OA=OC=OB=OD, \\
Since $\angle ADB=38^\circ$, \\
it implies $\angle BCA=\angle DBC=38^\circ$, \\
Since CE=BD, \\
it leads to AC=CE, \\
Therefore, $\angle E=\boxed{19^\circ}$

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a rectangle, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right; BC is extended to the right to E, so B, C, E are collinear and E is to the right of C. Segment AE connects from A diagonally down to the right to E, and intersects diagonal BD at F, and intersects side CD at G. The required ∠E is the angle formed by AE and EC at point E.
Reasoning: Draw auxiliary diagonal AC according to the method. Because ABCD is a rectangle, the two diagonals are equal, namely AC=BD. The problem statement gives CE=BD, therefore AC=CE. Also because in the rectangle AD ∥ BC, and diagonals AC and BD form corresponding acute angles with respect to the horizontal sides of the rectangle, ∠BCA=∠ADB=38°. Since CE is the reverse extension line of CB, ∠ACE=180°−38°=142°. In triangle ACE, AC=CE, therefore it is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠CAE and ∠AEC are equal. Thus ∠E=∠AEC=(180°−142°)/2=19°.
